title: Declarative Question 陳述式問句
titleEn: Using declarative questions for confirmation, surprise or follow-up

source.file: Sentence Structure 155 -「Declarative Question 陳述式問句」.pdf
omissions: English versions of Chinese-only Important Rules are faithful editorial translations.

formula: Subject + verb / auxiliary verb + other information + ?

formulas.formula: Subject + verb / auxiliary verb + other information + ?

rules.zh: 保留陳述句語序 一般問句通常把助動詞放在主語之前： 陳述式問句不使用這種倒裝：
rules.en: Keep statement word order. A standard question normally places the auxiliary before the subject, as in Did you call her? A declarative question does not use this inversion: You called her?

rules.zh: 必要時移除 do、does 或 did 當一般問句使用 do、does 或 did 時，改寫後通常要移除這些助動詞，並把主要動詞改成正確形 式。
rules.en: Remove do, does or did when necessary. When a standard question uses one of these auxiliaries, the declarative question normally removes it and changes the main verb to the correct form: Does Ben work here? becomes Ben works here?; Did Emma leave early? becomes Emma left early?

rules.zh: be 動詞、情態動詞及完成式助動詞放在主語後
rules.en: Keep be verbs, modal verbs and perfect auxiliaries after the subject be Is she coming? She is coming? Can you swim? You can swim? Have they finished? They have finished?

rules.zh: 使用上揚語調 在說話時，句尾聲調通常上揚，讓聽者知道這是一條問題，而不是普通陳述句。
rules.en: Use rising intonation. In speech, the voice normally rises at the end so that the listener recognises the utterance as a question rather than an ordinary statement.

rules.zh: 主要用於確認、驚訝或追問 陳述式問句通常表示說話者已經聽到、看到或猜到某些資料，現在想確認是否正確。 這句通常表示說話者對「你勝出了」感到驚訝，並希望確認消息。
rules.en: Use declarative questions mainly for confirmation, surprise or follow-up questions. They normally show that the speaker has heard, seen or guessed some information and now wants to check whether it is correct. You won the competition? usually expresses surprise at the news and asks for confirmation.

rules.zh: 較常用於對話 陳述式問句常見於日常對話、電影對白及即時追問。正式問卷、正式訪問或需要完全中立地索取 資料時，一般問句通常較合適。
rules.en: Declarative questions are more common in conversation, film dialogue and immediate follow-up questions. Standard questions are generally more suitable in formal questionnaires or interviews, or when requesting information in a completely neutral way.

benefits.zh: 幫助你迅速確認資料 當別人剛剛告訴你一件事時，你可以直接重複重點並加上問號，不需要重新組織一條完整的一般 問句。 （會議已經取消了？）
benefits.en: It helps you confirm information quickly. When someone has just told you something, you can repeat the key information with a question mark instead of reorganising it as a full standard question: The meeting has been cancelled?

benefits.zh: 自然表達驚訝 陳述式問句可以讓聽者立即感受到你對消息感到意外。 （你一直步行回家？）
benefits.en: It shows surprise naturally. A declarative question lets the listener immediately hear that the news has surprised you: You walked all the way home?
examples: You walked all the way home?

benefits.zh: 令追問聽起來更像自然對話 當你正在與別人交談時，這個句型可以讓追問簡短、直接，不會像正式訪問問題一樣生硬。
benefits.en: It makes follow-up questions sound conversational. During a conversation, the structure keeps a follow-up short and direct without making it sound as stiff as a formal interview question.

benefits.zh: 表示你對答案已有一定猜測 一般問句可以完全中立地索取資料，而陳述式問句通常表示你已經相信某件事可能是真的，只是 希望對方確認。 Compare 比較： （你讀完整本書了嗎？） 這是一條較中立的一般問題。 （你讀完整本書了？） 這句帶有確認或驚訝的語氣。
benefits.en: It shows that you already have an idea of the answer. A standard question can request information neutrally, whereas a declarative question normally suggests that you already think something may be true and only want confirmation. Did you finish the whole book? is neutral; You finished the whole book? conveys confirmation or surprise.
examples: Did you finish the whole book?
